behavior: Forages mainly by plunge-diving headfirst for schooling fish, then drains water from its throat pouch before swallowing. Social birds often glide low over the water in lines or V formations and nest in colonies.
field_marks: Huge, stocky seabird with a slender neck and an extremely long, grayish bill with a hooked tip and expandable throat pouch.
Adults have a white head washed pale yellow; breeding birds develop a rich reddish-brown neck.
Silver-gray and brown-streaked upperparts contrast with a dark brown belly; immatures are browner with pale underparts.
Adult irises range from pale blue to yellowish white and become brown during the breeding season; juvenile irises are dark brown.
Long, broad wings appear bowed in a glide and end in separated, fingerlike dark flight feathers.
Short dark tail and short black legs with fully webbed feet.
habitat: Coastal marine and estuarine waters, especially shallow bays, beaches, and nearshore waters. Roosts on sandbars, pilings, jetties, mangroves, and offshore rocks; nests colonially on secluded islands or coastal vegetation.
